title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): Tate's theorem (Driebergen 1966) says that if S is a noetherian normal integral scheme whose function field k(η) has characteristic 0, then restriction BT(S) → BT(η) of Barsotti–Tate (p-divisible) groups is fully faithful. A BT group on S is therefore determined, up to unique isomorphism, by its p-adic Galois representation. Grothendieck adds that the hypothesis char k(η) = 0 should be unnecessary. On this page he isolates the remaining case: char k(η) = L = p, the equal-characteristic case.

Proposed strategy in modern language:
(1) Assume 'Problem 1', presumably a good crystalline Dieudonné theory. Then BT groups over a characteristic-p base become Dieudonné F-crystals: locally free crystals on the crystalline site with Frobenius and Verschiebung. Hom of BT groups should then equal Hom of Dieudonné crystals.
(2) New problem: for S noetherian, normal, integral of characteristic p with generic point η, is restriction Cris_loc_lib(S) → Cris_loc_lib(η) fully faithful? He hedges: 'or at least the analogous functor for F-crystals'.
(3) Reduction. By normality, morphisms extend across codimension ≥ 2, so one passes to height-one localizations (DVRs). One then completes and makes the residue field algebraically closed, reaching S = Spec k[[t]] with k algebraically closed. There a crystal is a finite free W(k)[[t]]-module with an integrable, topologically quasi-nilpotent connection. Over the generic point it becomes a module with connection over the p-adic completion of W(k)[[t]][1/t] (or a Cohen ring of k((t))). Full faithfulness then means: a horizontal (Frobenius-compatible) morphism defined generically has coefficients in W[[t]].
(4) Also needed: Dieudonné theory over a perfect ring, with an equivalence of categories. This handles the generic point, e.g. after passing to the perfection of k((t)) and descending. With (2) and (4), Tate's theorem in equal characteristic follows: Hom(G,H) → Hom(G_η,H_η) is bijective.

This is precisely the programme later carried out by A. J. de Jong ('Homomorphisms of Barsotti–Tate groups and crystals in positive characteristic', Invent. Math. 1998). That paper uses crystalline Dieudonné theory over bases with p-bases and full faithfulness of F-crystals over k[[t]] → k((t)).
errors: Without Frobenius the question as first posed (all locally free crystals) has a negative answer in general. A horizontal section over the generic point (solution of a p-adic differential equation over the completion of W[[t]][1/t]) need not extend to W[[t]]; rank-one connections with non-convergent solutions give examples. Grothendieck's hedge 'du moins pour F-cristaux' is the correct version, and that is what de Jong proved.

The reduction to k[[t]] with k algebraically closed is 'facile' only modulo care with imperfect residue fields and descent from the algebraic closure; Grothendieck glosses over this. Likewise the generic point k((t)) is not perfect, so Dieudonné theory over a perfect ring needs a descent step that is not mentioned.
Minor: the parenthesis '(avec équivalence de catégories' is never closed.

ideas.what: Conjecture that Tate's full-faithfulness theorem for BT groups (normal base, restriction to generic point) holds in equal characteristic p.
ideas.modern_name: Tate's theorem for p-divisible groups in characteristic p (de Jong's theorem)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Conjectured by Grothendieck; proved by A. J. de Jong (1998)
ideas.where_published: Possibly in Grothendieck, 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux' (ICM Nice 1970) / Montréal notes 1974 (unsure)

ideas.what: Full faithfulness of restriction of locally free (F-)crystals from S to its generic point; reduction to k[[t]] and formulation via modules with formal connections.
ideas.modern_name: Full faithfulness of restriction for F-crystals / F-isocrystals (de Jong; Kedlaya for overconvergent F-isocrystals)
ideas.usually_credited_to: A. J. de Jong (1998); K. Kedlaya (2004) for the isocrystal version

ideas.what: Strategy: Dieudonné theory over a perfect ring (with equivalence) plus F-crystal extension implies Tate's theorem in characteristic p.
ideas.modern_name: Dieudonné theory over perfect rings; crystalline Dieudonné functor full faithfulness
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gabber (unpublished), Berthelot (perfect valuation rings 1980), Lau (2013); de Jong (full faithfulness over bases with p-basis)
ideas.where_published: Problem list in Montréal notes possibly

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates the exact reduction later used to prove Tate's theorem in characteristic p: Dieudonné theory, then full faithfulness of F-crystal restriction over k[[t]] → k((t)). This predates de Jong by roughly 25 years. It was taken up and finished (de Jong 1998), so it is not missed mathematically, but it documents the strategy's origin.
missed.quote: Il semble que si la réponse au Pb précédent est affirmative, et si on sait faire la théorie de Dieudonné sur un anneau parfait (avec équivalence de catégories alors on aura démonstration du th. de Tate en égales car.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical attribution of the problem and strategy behind de Jong's theorem. No new mathematics beyond the published literature.

deep.surprise_reason: A clear, correct, early formulation of what became de Jong's theorem and its proof strategy. The conjecture itself is likely known as a Grothendieck problem, and the whole programme has since been carried out.
